title: Guided tour
note: Single source of truth for the tour. Targets are tried in order: data-tour first, then data-action fallbacks. 'before' runs only whitelisted, local, read-only UI actions (see tour.js ACTIONS). 'demoOnly' steps are skipped when signed in.

steps.title: Welcome to Health Expo Passport
steps.body: This tour shows every part of the app using the three made-up demo visitors. It changes nothing in your church's database. Use Next and Back, or press Escape to pause. You can pick it up again from Profile → Settings & help.

steps.title: Home: who is being screened now
steps.body: The top card is the visitor whose checks are open, with their key readings. Tap the name to switch to another visitor.

steps.title: Help on every screen
steps.body: The ? button opens the help for the screen you are on. It works in practice mode too.

steps.title: Practice mode or live
steps.body: The cloud button shows sync status. In practice mode it opens “Sync & sign-in”: sign in there to work a real expo with your church.

steps.title: Today's visitors
steps.body: Each row is a visitor, coloured green, amber or red by their readings. Tap a row to continue their passport. The bin removes a demo visitor.

steps.title: The six tabs
steps.body: The bottom bar is the whole app: Home, Visitor, Queue, Care, Team and Profile. The numbers are counts, such as people waiting in the queue.

steps.title: Step 1 — Register
steps.body: Every visit starts here: Register a new visitor, with their name, age, sex and their consent (POPIA). In the tour we use the demo visitor David instead.

steps.title: The Visitor tab
steps.body: Visitor holds one person's passport and the four steps of a visit.

steps.title: Step 2 — Check
steps.body: Each station records its readings here. The checks open one at a time, like a short form: answer, then Next → or Enter. Volunteers pick Your station so they only see their own check. If they are still waiting in that station's line, the app asks whether to start serving them.

steps.title: Checks: one at a time
steps.body: The bar shows Check n of 8. Back keeps your answers, Skip leaves a check for later, and the summary lists all 8. Prefer the paper-style form? Tap Show all 8 checks; One at a time brings you back.

steps.title: Step 3 — Results
steps.body: Confirm the readings and see the health age. The health age is an estimate to start a conversation, not a diagnosis. Opening Results marks a station still serving them as done.

steps.title: Step 4 — Plan
steps.body: A 90-day healthy-living plan is built from the readings. Your church can add its own plans.

steps.title: Step 5 — Send home
steps.body: Send the plan by WhatsApp or email, or print a card. You always see a preview first.

steps.title: Step 6 — Finish the visit
steps.body: Finish visit ✓ takes the visitor out of every queue and returns you to Home. (We won't press it in the tour.)

steps.title: The Queue
steps.body: One line per station. Every desk sees the same line when signed in; in practice mode the line is only on this phone.

steps.title: Pick a station
steps.body: Tap a station card to see who is waiting there. Vitals & BMI has two demo visitors waiting.

steps.title: Try it: Call next
steps.body: Tap Call next to call the first person in the Vitals line. This is practice data on this phone only. (Or tap Next to skip.)

steps.title: Done · call next
steps.body: When their check is done, Done · call next marks them finished here and sends them on to their next station. ↩ Put back returns someone to their place; ✕ removes them.

steps.title: Several people at once
steps.body: If a station serves more than one person at a time (3 blood-pressure nurses, 2 prayer partners), tap + next to People served at once. Each place gets its own card with the person, start time and minutes; a free place shows Call next → Place 2. ⇄ moves someone to another place and Name places labels them (Nurse A, Room 2). The big screen then shows Serving 2 of 3.

steps.title: Big screen
steps.body: Shows who is being served and who is next, for a TV at the expo. A station with several places lists each place and Serving 2 of 3. ✕ or Escape closes it.

steps.title: Care: follow-up after the expo
steps.body: The team works from these lists after the screenings: Urgent first, then the 48-hour calls, then interests. Once someone has been phoned or sent to a clinic, Called / attended to ✓ takes them out of the red number on Care. The WhatsApp button opens a message to the visitor.

steps.title: Export CSV holds personal data
steps.body: The export contains health information. The app asks where to send it; keep the file private and delete it when you are done. Minimal CSV leaves out names, contacts and prayer notes; Excel gives a formatted sheet; the prayer list is a separate file.

steps.title: Team: volunteers
steps.body: Pledge to help, see who stands where (Muster and Booth), and log expo hours (Record). If you are a volunteer, start on Pledge.

steps.title: Booths and team leaders
steps.body: Booth shows each station's helpers. A team leader leads one booth and can place helpers there.

steps.title: Profile and settings
steps.body: Your account and sync status. Signed in, it has three sections: Pledge (helping at an expo), My details (your details and results) and Account (password, help, sign out).

steps.title: Settings & help
steps.body: Help & tutorial opens the full guide. Take the guided tour brings you back here at any time, to resume or start again. Queue: people served at once jumps to the station places setting.

steps.title: Practice mode vs live
steps.body: Practice mode uses made-up visitors; nothing is sent to your church's database and demo data stays on this phone until you tap Reset demo. Sign in to work a real expo. Never enter real visitors in practice mode.

steps.title: Who does what
steps.body: Volunteer or team member: works a station. Team leader: leads one booth and places its helpers. The Health Department Leader and their Assistant run the church: they approve people, set up expos, write plans and export data. Someone joining picks their church first, then their position, and the church approves it.

steps.title: Privacy and how long data is kept
steps.body: Only your church's admins and the staff they approve see visitor records. Readings and prayer notes are deleted 7 days after the visit. If a visitor agrees to follow-up, only their name and contact details are kept, for up to 2 years. Visitors may ask to see, correct or delete their data (POPIA).

steps.title: If a reading is red
steps.body: Red means a reading is in the danger range. Stay calm and kind. Tell the counselling or health lead now, and encourage a clinic visit soon. For chest pain, stroke signs, fainting or a very low sugar, call for emergency help straight away.
steps.extra: [PLACEHOLDER — church health lead to confirm before the expo] Ambulance 10177 · Emergency from a cellphone 112

steps.title: You're ready
steps.body: That's the whole app. Practise as much as you like with the demo visitors. Take the tour again from Profile → Settings & help.
